# Module 1: Vector Spaces & Cosine Similarity with NumPy
import numpy as np
from sentence_transformers import SentenceTransformer

# 1. Load lightweight 80MB embedding model (384-dimensional vector space)
embedder = SentenceTransformer("sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2")

# 2. Target query and food review corpus
query = "Spicy Karachi beef biryani with lots of aloo and aroma"
reviews = [
    "Hot spicy beef biryani with succulent potatoes and golden rice.",
    "Mild chicken yakhni pulao with cardamom and delicate spices.",
    "Sweet carrot halwa with desi ghee, almonds, and pistachios.",
    "Crisp fried fish with tangy lemon garlic tartar sauce."
]

# 3. Vectorize text into 2D NumPy float32 matrix
query_vec = embedder.encode(query)
corpus_vecs = embedder.encode(reviews)

# 4. Pure NumPy SIMD Cosine Similarity: (A . B) / (||A|| * ||B||)
dot_products = np.dot(corpus_vecs, query_vec)
norms = np.linalg.norm(corpus_vecs, axis=1) * np.linalg.norm(query_vec)
similarities = dot_products / norms

print(f"Target Query: '{query}'\n" + "="*50)
for idx in np.argsort(-similarities):
    print(f"Score: {similarities[idx]:.4f} | Review: {reviews[idx]}")

# Module 4: Custom PyTorch Neural Network MLP trained on HF Dataset
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
from datasets import load_dataset
from transformers import AutoTokenizer

# 1. Load Tokenizer & Stream Dataset
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("distilbert/distilbert-base-uncased")
dataset = load_dataset("rotten_tomatoes", split="train", streaming=True)
batch = list(dataset.take(200))

# 2. Tokenize inputs into PyTorch Tensors
encodings = tokenizer([b["text"] for b in batch], padding=True, truncation=True, max_length=64, return_tensors="pt")
labels = torch.tensor([b["label"] for b in batch], dtype=torch.long)

# 3. Define 3-Layer Deep Neural Network with PyTorch nn.Module
class SentimentMLP(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, vocab_size=30522, embed_dim=32, hidden_dim=64):
        super().__init__()
        self.embedding = nn.Embedding(vocab_size, embed_dim)
        self.fc1 = nn.Linear(embed_dim, hidden_dim)
        self.relu = nn.ReLU()
        self.dropout = nn.Dropout(0.2)
        self.fc2 = nn.Linear(hidden_dim, 2)
    def forward(self, input_ids):
        x = self.embedding(input_ids).mean(dim=1)
        return self.fc2(self.dropout(self.relu(self.fc1(x))))

model = SentimentMLP()
optimizer = torch.optim.AdamW(model.parameters(), lr=0.01)
criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()

# 4. Run 5 Training Epochs with PyTorch Autograd
for epoch in range(5):
    optimizer.zero_grad()
    logits = model(encodings["input_ids"])
    loss = criterion(logits, labels)
    loss.backward()
    optimizer.step()
    acc = (logits.argmax(dim=1) == labels).float().mean()
    print(f"Epoch {epoch+1}/5 | CrossEntropy Loss: {loss.item():.4f} | Batch Accuracy: {acc*100:.1f}%")

# Module 5: Extracting and Inspecting Self-Attention Tensors in Transformers
import torch
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModelForCausalLM

# 1. Load GPT-2 with output_attentions enabled (100% Free on CPU)
model_name = "gpt2"
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name)
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(model_name, output_attentions=True)
model.eval()

# 2. Tokenize prompt sentence
text = "The Transformer attention mechanism replaced recurrence with parallel matrix math"
inputs = tokenizer(text, return_tensors="pt")
tokens = tokenizer.convert_ids_to_tokens(inputs["input_ids"][0])

# 3. Forward pass extracting Multi-Head Attention weights
with torch.no_grad():
    outputs = model(**inputs)

# Shape: (num_layers=12, batch=1, num_heads=12, seq_len, seq_len)
last_layer_attn = outputs.attentions[-1][0] # Shape: (12, seq_len, seq_len)
avg_attn_heads = last_layer_attn.mean(dim=0) # Average across 12 heads

# 4. Display which past tokens the final token attends to most!
last_token_idx = len(tokens) - 1
attended_weights = avg_attn_heads[last_token_idx].numpy()

print(f"Token: '{tokens[last_token_idx]}' attends to earlier tokens:")
for tok, weight in sorted(zip(tokens, attended_weights), key=lambda x: -x[1])[:5]:
    print(f"  -> '{tok:15s}': Attention Weight {weight:.4f}")
